# Problem 1

"Using flowGate, go ahead and create your own series of gates for either our data or your own for any cell populations that might interest you. Once done, save the GatingSet, and then successfully reload it. Add another gate, but intentionally misdraw it. Then proceed to visualize, identify and correct it, before saving again."

## Solution step by step

1. activate the libraries
2. get directory
3. read full path for fcs files
4. load fcs files into a cytoset
5. create a gating set from the cytoset
6. get the fluorophores into a variable (colnames followed by str_detect to exclude scatters and time)
7. apply a transformation:
  i) attribute the transformation function to an object
  ii) use transformerList() to apply the transformation  from the step prior to the fluorophores only from step 6.
  iii) apply transform() to pass the list of transformations created in the step prior.
8. use gs_gate_interactive(gs = gatingsetobject, filterID= "name of the gate", sample = 1, dims = list("parameter 1", "parameter 2"), subset="parent gate") to draw 1 gate 

**OR**

9. use a tibble to provide a sequential gating strategy
  * is it possible to create this outside of R environment, using a notepad or spreadsheet software?
10. save gating set
12. reload gating set
13. draw the wrong gate
14. visualize it using autoplot for one of the samples (as realistically there's when I'd notice it)
15. redraw *hint* use argument regate = TRUE in the gs_gate_interactive()
16. check the new gate was applied properly 
17. save correct gating set.


## Results

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
# libraries:
library(flowWorkspace)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggcyto)
library(stringr)
library(flowGate)

# directory
getwd()

# get location for the files and full path for the .fcs files
storage_location = file.path("data")
fcsfiles_path = list.files(storage_location, pattern = ".fcs", full.names = TRUE)
fcsfiles_path #confirming the paths are here


# create a cytoset with the fcs files:
cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(fcsfiles_path, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)

#create gating set:
gatingset = GatingSet(cytoset)
gatingset #gating set created

# get the fluorophore parameters:

parameters = colnames(gatingset)
fluorophore_parameters = parameters[!str_detect(parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]
fluorophore_parameters

# get the markers names as well:
marker_fluorophores = markernames(gatingset)
marker_fluorophores

# apply optimized bioexponential transformation:
bioexponential = flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144, pos=4.5, neg=2, widthBasis=-500)
biexp_transform = transformerList(fluorophore_parameters, bioexponential)
transform(gatingset, biexp_transform)
```

### Cell gate

I will draw a polygon gate for a "Cell" gate to exclude debris:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# draw a "cell" gate
gs_gate_interactive(gs=gatingset, filterId="cells", sample=1,
dims=list("FSC-A", "SSC-A"), subset="root")

# check that it applied to all specimens:
plot(gatingset)
gs_pop_get_count_fast(gatingset)

# or ggcyto
ggcyto(gatingset[1], subset="root",
 aes(x="FSC-A", y="SSC-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100) + geom_gate("cells") + theme_bw()
```

Let's design a sequential gating strategy.
For a set like this, this would be my strategy:
cells > singlets > 
live (FSC-A, Viability) > Lin neg CD45pos (CD45, Dump) > Tcells (CD3, SSC-A) > CD4pos vs CD8pos vs DN (CD4, CD8)
in CD4pos > Tregs (CD25pos FoxP3pos) vs FoxP3neg 

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# activate tibble
library (tibble)

# create a tibble:
gating_table = tribble(
  ~filterId,    ~dims,                          ~subset,      
  "Live",     list("FSC-A", "Viability"),          "singlets",      
  "CD45pos",       list("CD45", "Dump"),   "Live",  
  "Tcells",     list("CD3", "SSC-A"),              "CD45pos",     
  "CD4pos",       list("CD8", "CD4"),               "Tcells",   
  "CD8pos",       list("CD8", "CD4"),               "Tcells",   
  "DN",         list("CD8", "CD4"),                "Tcells",
  "Tregs",      list("CD25", "FoxP3"),             "CD4pos",
  "FoxP3neg",   list("CD25", "FoxP3"),             "CD4pos",
)

gating_table
str(gating_table) # checking that everything is ok

#apply gating strategy to the gatingset
gs_apply_gating_strategy(gatingset, gating_strategy = gating_table)

autoplot(gatingset[[1]]) + theme_bw()
autoplot(gatingset[[4]])

ggcyto(gatingset[1], subset="CD4pos",
 aes(x="CD25", y="FoxP3")) + geom_hex(bins=100) + geom_gate(c("Tregs", "FoxP3neg")) + theme_bw()
```

# Problem 2

"Go ahead and create your own openCyto gate template, extending to whatever cell target population of interest. Visualize the differences, and ensure that the gates are correctly applied for everyone. Set gate_constraint arguments as needed until everything is just right."

## Solution step by step

1. activate the libraries
2. get or set directory
3. read full path for fcs files
4. load fcs files into a cytoset
5. create a gating set from the cytoset
6. get the fluorophores into a variable (colnames followed by str_detect to exclude scatters and time)
7. apply a transformation:
  i) attribute the transformation function to an object
  ii) use transformerList() to apply the transformation  from the step prior to the fluorophores only from step 6.
  iii) apply transform() to pass the list of transformations created in the step prior.
8. visualize some of the plots with ggcyto() for some parameters from which I'd like to plot to see what type of gate would make sense and try to get idea for gating_args
  i) I will create this .csv file outside of R and read it into R environment using fread()
9. load the gatingTemplate into R
10. apply gating template to an object *hint* use gatingTemplate()
11. apply gating template to the gatingset *hint* gt_gating()
12. visualize gates using autoplot().
13. correct any gates by changing values gating_args as needed.
14. save the gating set for the next problem.



```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# activate the libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggcyto)
library(flowWorkspace)
library(openCyto)
library(stringr)
library(data.table)

# get directoruy, store location path and files:
getwd()
storage_location = file.path("data")
fcs_files = list.files (storage_location, pattern=".fcs", full.names=TRUE)
fcs_files

# create a cytoset with the fcs files:
cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(fcs_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)

#create gating set:
gatingset = GatingSet(cytoset)
gatingset #gating set created

# get the fluorophore parameters:

parameters = colnames(gatingset)
fluorophore_parameters = parameters[!str_detect(parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]
fluorophore_parameters

# get the markers names as well:
marker_fluorophores = markernames(gatingset)
marker_fluorophores

# apply optimized bioexponential transformation:
bioexponential = flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144, pos=4.5, neg=2, widthBasis=-500)
biexp_transform = transformerList(fluorophore_parameters, bioexponential)
transform(gatingset, biexp_transform)
```
Gating strategy:

cells (flowClust) > singlets (singletGate) > live (flowClust)> CD45+ (gate_mindensity)> Dump- (gate_mindensity)> Tcells (gate_mindensity) > CD4 (flowClust) > CD62L (gate_mindensity) 
Tcells > CD8 (flowClust)

```{r}

# check CD4 vs CD8 
ggcyto(gatingset[2], subset="root",
 aes(x="CD4", y="CD8")) + geom_hex(bins=100) + theme_bw()
```

flowClust takes 2 gating_args, the target for CD4 should be c(3.5e4, 2e4); CD8 should be c(2e4, 3.75e4)

## Final thoughts:

I think autogating is great for those black and white populationsm, where there is clear definition for neg and pos populations. 

And even then, when I tried using flowClust in a CD4 vs CD8 it couldn't do it properly and resulted in a terrible merge of both populations. I'm thinking that's most likely due to the fact flowClust is not suitable for this kind of separation and just overides whatever was drawn first or adds to the 1st gate it created. 

openCyto has more gating methods that would probably be more suitable for this endeavour. Maybe a quadGate.tmix would work (I'll explore this later.)


# Problem 3

"Re-run your openCyto template, but then add a few additional flowGate on to to extend it further. Save the gating set, close out of positron, and successfully reload."

## Solution
1. activate the libraries needed.
2. get or set directory
3. load gs file from problem 2. 
4. add a manual gate using the flowGate library related functions.
5. save the gating set. 
6. reload it after closing positron.
7. check the gates inside the gatinset and visualize the plots!


## Results


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
# libraries:
library(flowWorkspace)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggcyto)
library(flowGate)
library(openCyto)
library(dplyr)

# directory
getwd()

#get gs files:
storage_location = file.path("data")
gsfiles_path = list.files(storage_location, pattern=".gs", full.names=TRUE)
gsfiles_path

#load gs file:
problem2_gs = load_gs(gsfiles_path[6])

# check if it looks the same as before:
plot(problem2_gs)
stats = gs_pop_get_count_fast(problem2_gs)
stats
```

Successfully reloading gs allowed me to recover the full gating strategy from gating set saved in problem 2:

![](/course/08_WaysToGate/homeworks/alexandragabrielaferreira/images/problem3_reload_gs.png)

Let's correct the CD62L gate manually and confirm the gate is applied to the full gating set:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# regate CD62Lpos population to correct it using a SEB sample:
gs_gate_interactive(gs=problem2_gs, filterId="CD62Lpos", sample=6,
dims=list("CD62L", "SSC-A"), subset="CD4pos", regate=TRUE)

# confirming gate is good for control and SEB samples:
autoplot(problem2_gs[[1]]) + theme_bw()
autoplot(problem2_gs[[2]]) + theme_bw()

# or with ggcyto:

## SEB sample
ggcyto(problem2_gs[4], subset="CD4pos",
 aes(x="CD62L", y="SSC-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100) + geom_gate("CD62Lpos")theme_bw()

## SEB sample
ggcyto(problem2_gs[4], subset="CD4pos",
 aes(x="CD62L", y="SSC-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100) + geom_gate("CD62Lpos") + theme_bw()

## Cntrl sample:
ggcyto(problem2_gs[3], subset="CD4pos",
 aes(x="CD62L", y="SSC-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100) + geom_gate("CD62Lpos") + theme_bw()

plot(problem2_gs)
gs_pop_get_count_fast(problem2_gs) |> filter(Population %in% "/Cells/Singlets/Live/CD45pos/Tcells/CD4pos/CD62Lpos")
```

From this exercise I successfully reloaded a gating set saved on the day before from problem 2 and manually regated a problematic gate generated from the autogating strategy I did in problem 2.
